title: Gyeran Mari Rolled Omelet
shortDescription: Thin layers of beaten egg with scallion and carrot are rolled in a skillet, then sliced into neat spirals.
culturalContext: Gyeran mari is a Korean rolled-egg dish served as banchan, in lunch boxes, or with drinks. Fillings, seasoning, thickness, and rolling technique vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

instructions.heading: Mix the eggs
instructions.action: Beat eggs with salt, then stir in scallion and carrot.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The whites and yolks are combined without large streaks.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash hands after handling raw egg and keep the mixture off ready-to-eat foods.

instructions.heading: Preheat gently
instructions.action: Heat the skillet over medium-low and wipe in a thin film of oil.

instructions.heading: Start the roll
instructions.action: Pour a thin layer of egg; when mostly set but still glossy on top, roll it toward one side.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The layer bends without flowing raw egg.

instructions.heading: Build layers
instructions.action: Oil the exposed pan lightly, add another thin layer under the roll, and roll again; repeat until the egg is used.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The roll is firm, layered, and lightly golden.
instructions.safetyNote: Control heat so the exterior does not burn before the center cooks.

instructions.heading: Verify doneness
instructions.action: Check the center with a clean thermometer and continue turning gently until it reaches 160°F / 71°C.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The center reaches 160°F / 71°C and no liquid egg remains.

instructions.heading: Rest and slice
instructions.action: Rest 5 minutes, then slice on a clean board with a clean knife.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this egg roll is cooked in a skillet.
targetInternalTemperature: 160°F / 71°C in the center of the finished egg roll.
visualDonenessCues: Layers are set with no liquid egg
Roll is firm enough to slice
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw egg separate from ready-to-eat foods.
Cook the center of the egg roll to 160°F / 71°C.
Use a clean board and knife for the cooked roll.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains egg; use clean cookware and utensils to manage cross-contact.

substitutions: Finely chopped chives may replace scallion.
Omit carrot rather than using large wet fillings.
makeAhead: Cook up to 1 day ahead, cool promptly, cover, and refrigerate.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours in a covered container and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat gently until steaming, or serve properly refrigerated slices cool.
leftovers: Pack only properly chilled leftovers with an ice source.
servingSuggestions: Serve sliced as banchan or in a lunch box.

faq.question: Why is my roll breaking?
faq.answer: The layer may be too cooked, too thick, or overfilled; test cooking must calibrate the pan.

faq.question: Can the center stay soft?
faq.answer: It may stay tender, but the egg dish still must reach 160°F / 71°C.
